_comment: The settings, in the order the menu shows them, read by the web (src/ui/settingsTable.ts) and Godot (SettingsSheet). Each row: id, section, an optional group (a sub-header inside the section, drawn where it changes), name, a one-line hint, its control (toggle, slider, select, button, or panel: a web panel of its own, like the frame rate), and for sliders min/max/step, for selects options (or none: the view fills them in). `only` keeps a row to one of the two (web or godot); `when` shows it only where it applies (installedAndroid: the app installed on Android; devBuild: the dev server or a PR preview). Defaults for the plain settings; graphics take theirs from the preset.

fps._comment: The frame rate watch (#391), read by the web (src/view/fps.ts) and Godot (Fps.cs): one reading a second, the last `history` kept; 'low' is the middle of the last `seconds` readings under `low` (Settings advises), 'veryLow' under `veryLow` (the game itself offers one click to lighter graphics).

auto._comment: Automatic graphics (#591, web only for now: src/view/autoGraphics.ts). On the title, every reading of the last `titleSeconds` under `low` drops an exact preset straight to Low. Anywhere, on Low or Medium, the slowest tenth of the last `raiseSeconds` readings at `nearCap` of the display's cap (the highest reading seen, at least `minCap`) steps up one preset; for `watchSeconds` after that, the middle of the last `seconds` readings under `fallBack` of the cap steps back and stops raising for good.
